name: Generator sales, rental and service

problems.words: I do not know exactly which generator is on which site right now
quick_ideas: Make one list of every unit with its status (yard, on hire, under repair) and site area, so the fleet is visible in one place
Update it every time a unit moves, so it stays true.

workzap_build.text: dashboards_reports — A rental fleet register showing each unit's capacity, status, site area and due-back date, updated from dispatch and return checks.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how many units are in your rental fleet?
problems.free_stops: Register fields and update flow are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk the yard and compare the units physically present with the latest dispatch notes, so missing location updates stand out quickly.
Give one dispatcher the job of updating one movement notebook whenever a unit leaves, arrives, or enters repair, so everyone checks the same place.

problems.words: Units come back off-hire late but the bill stops on the agreed date
quick_ideas: Record the actual return date on every off-hire, so billing uses the real date
List units past their due-back date every Monday, so overdue hires are chased.

workzap_build.text: Hire billing from actual out and in dates with automatic alerts for overdue returns.

problems.ask_first: Do hires come back late on most contracts, or only a few?
problems.free_stops: Billing rules are in the solution document; pi gives no advice on what to charge.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many off-hire units returned after the agreed date this week, so lost billing days become visible.
Give the yard return check to one person with one notebook for actual return dates, so billing uses what really happened.

problems.words: Rental units come back damaged or with less fuel and we cannot prove the condition when they left
quick_ideas: Take photos and note running hours and fuel level at every dispatch, so there is a starting record
Get the customer's site contact to sign at delivery and return, so both sides agree.

workzap_build.text: An on-hire and off-hire checklist on phone with photos, running hours and fuel level, compared automatically at return.

problems.ask_first: Is the trouble mostly fuel level, mostly damage, or both?
problems.free_stops: Checklist items are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare return notes with dispatch notes for recent hires, so you see how often condition and fuel details are missing.
Give one yard person the dispatch record book for every outgoing rental unit, so condition notes are written before it leaves.

problems.words: Breakdown calls come at night and nobody knows which technician is free
quick_ideas: Set a written on-call rota for nights and weekends, so there is always a named person
Note the time each breakdown call came in and was attended, so response times are on record.

workzap_build.text: booking_scheduling — Breakdown call intake via WhatsApp with technician assignment from the on-call rota, response time and closure.

problems.ask_first: Do night calls come every week, or only during storms and long power cuts?
problems.free_stops: Intake flow and rota logic are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which night breakdown calls waited while staff checked who was available, so the delay from unclear cover is clear.
Give one supervisor the nightly technician availability list in one notebook, so breakdown calls go straight to the right person.

problems.words: AMC customers complain the PM visit never happened
quick_ideas: List every active AMC with its next PM due date, so visits are planned, not remembered
Get a customer sign-off at every visit, so you have proof it happened.

workzap_build.text: field_checks — A PM schedule by running hours or dates per AMC customer, with reminders and visit sign-off on phone.

problems.ask_first: Is it a few contracts with missed visits, or most of them?
problems.free_stops: Schedule rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare planned PM visits due this week with signed job sheets received, so missed AMC visits are easy to spot.
Give one coordinator the AMC visit list and a fixed afternoon check for missing sign-offs, so skipped visits are chased quickly.

problems.words: We forget AMC renewals and the customer goes elsewhere
quick_ideas: Add the renewal date to the AMC list, so expiries are visible
Contact customers well before expiry, so renewal is a conversation, not a surprise.

workzap_build.text: AMC renewal reminders and a renewal pipeline showing which contracts are due, in talks or lost.

problems.ask_first: Do you lose customers mostly at renewal time, or earlier when a visit is missed?
problems.free_stops: Reminder timing is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many AMC contracts expire soon without any renewal note beside them, so the renewal miss is visible early.
Give one person one renewal notebook and a fixed weekly review of upcoming AMC expiries, so customers are approached before they drift away.

problems.words: Technicians report jobs done but I do not see job sheets for days
quick_ideas: Ask for a photo of each signed job sheet the same day, so the office knows it is done
Check open job sheets each morning, so nothing sits for a week.

workzap_build.text: Digital job sheets with parts used, linked to stock deduction and visible to the office as soon as they are closed.

problems.ask_first: Do job sheets come late from every technician, or mainly from those working far away?
problems.free_stops: Job sheet design is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note the days between each completed job and the office receiving its job sheet, so the reporting delay is measurable.
Give one technician on each shift the handover job of bringing all completed job sheets to one desk before leaving, so paperwork stops piling up.

problems.words: Filters and spare parts are out when a breakdown happens
quick_ideas: List the parts used most often in breakdowns, so you know what must never run out
Set a minimum for each and check it weekly, so you reorder in time.

workzap_build.text: Spare parts stock with minimum levels and alerts, with import or supplier order tracking.

problems.ask_first: Is it a few common parts running out, or a wide range of parts?
problems.free_stops: Minimum levels and tracking are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Look at recent breakdown jobs and note which filters or parts were missing at the moment of need, so repeat shortages are clear.
Give one storekeeper one shelf list and a fixed weekly stock check for fast-moving breakdown parts, so shortages are caught before the next call.

problems.words: I have no idea if a rental unit earns more than it costs in maintenance
quick_ideas: Total hire income and repair cost per unit for the last few months, so you see which units carry the fleet
Mark the units that keep coming back for the same fault, so repeat costs stand out.

workzap_build.text: Fleet utilisation and earnings against maintenance cost per unit, with a repeat-fault report.

problems.ask_first: Do you rent out mostly a few large units, or many small ones?
problems.free_stops: Cost allocation is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each rental unit's recent hire days with its recent maintenance notes, so units with heavy upkeep stand out.
Give one person one notebook page per rental unit for hire days and maintenance spend, so weak earners stop being mixed with stronger ones.

problems.words: Corporate customers pay rental and service invoices very late
quick_ideas: List every unpaid invoice with its age, so you know who to chase first
Send statements on a fixed day each month, so payment has a rhythm.

workzap_build.text: A receivables tracker with statements and automatic reminders by customer.

problems.ask_first: Is it a few big corporate customers owing most, or many paying late?
problems.free_stops: Reminder rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which unpaid corporate invoices are waiting on timesheets, purchase orders, or approvals, so you see what is slowing each payment.
Give one staff member a fixed weekly slot to chase every unpaid rental and service invoice from one notebook, so follow-up stays consistent.

problems.words: Event rentals booked on WhatsApp get double-booked
quick_ideas: Keep one booking calendar for all event units, so every booking is checked against it
Confirm a booking only once it is on the calendar.

workzap_build.text: An event booking calendar that blocks clashes and confirms bookings to the customer.

problems.ask_first: Do double bookings come up mostly on weekends, or whenever two people take bookings?
problems.free_stops: Calendar set-up is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare this week's event bookings against units already promised out, so clashes are spotted before trucks are arranged.
Give one person the job of writing every event booking in one shared list before promising availability, so the same unit is not promised twice.

never_say: Anything on generator sizing, wiring, earthing, load calculations, exhaust, ventilation or fuel storage.
Anything that helps with grid tapping, illegal connections, bypassing meters or avoiding environmental or noise rules.
Anything on what to charge for rental or service.
Anything that helps under-invoice or misdeclare imports.
Anything other than emergency services when carbon monoxide, fire, shock or explosion is described.

sample_reply.person: Our rental units come back with less fuel and damaged panels and we can never prove it. What can we do?
sample_reply.pi: Yes, this is fixable, and you can start this week on your own. 1) Take photos and note running hours and fuel level every time a unit leaves the yard, so there is a starting record. 2) Get the site contact to sign at delivery and at return, so both sides agree on the condition. Workzap can do this automatically for you: a dispatch and return checklist on phone that compares the two records for every unit and shows you which hires came back short. Shall I have a solution document and quote prepared for you? You are free to say no.
